label: L12 · Descriptive vs Analytic
rows: DISTRIBUTION by person, place, time → FORMULATES hypotheses. Design: community health survey (cross-sectional).
TESTS a specific hypothesis (exposure → outcome) → cause-effect. Designs: cohort, case-control, experimental.
Descriptive = PERSON, PLACE, TIME (do it first). Analytic = HOST, AGENT, ENVIRONMENT.
Point source (localized, stationary) · propagated (spreading) · seasonal · SECULAR (over years). Clustered = epidemic; even = endemic.

Agents: biological, physical, chemical, environmental, psychological. Host: genes, immune status, behavior, definitive vs intermediate. Environment: living conditions, climate, vector/vehicle/reservoir.
SPOT MAP of cases + pumps → Pump A; brewery with its own deep well spared → pump closed, outbreak ended.
Lambeth moved intake UPSTREAM; water source of every house with a death: Southwark and Vauxhall 4.2 vs Lambeth 0.5 per 1,000. No knowledge of microbes.

label: L12 · Uses, History & Genomics
rows: Epi (upon) + demos (people) + ology. Occurrence and distribution of health events in populations, their determinants, and APPLYING it to control.
What = event/diagnosis · Who = person/population · Where · When · WHY = causes, risk factors, modes of transmission.
Outbreak response · surveillance · communication · disease prioritization (who gets it, who dies, outcome) · training · experimental epidemiology · program evaluation (vaccine and clinical trials).
Hippocrates: rational, not spiritual · Graunt: tabulated mortality rates · FARR: father of modern VITAL STATISTICS · SNOW: father of FIELD epidemiology.
Doll and Hill: smoking and lung cancer · Framingham: multigenerational cardiovascular study · smallpox eradication · injuries/violence · bioterrorism.
Monitoring pathogens' GENETIC MAKEUP (sequencing): closely related = same outbreak; transmission links; sources of exposure; links cases in different places.

label: L12 · Data, Surveillance & Reporting
rows: Individuals (surveys: national nutrition survey) · environment (stream samples, air quality) · providers (meningitis notifications) · nonhealth (cigarette SALES, intoxicated-driver ARRESTS).
SYSTEMATIC collection, analysis, interpretation → prevention and control. Needs a clear objective.
Timeliness (control) · representation (temporal trend) · SENSITIVITY (find the sick) · SPECIFICITY (exclude the well).
ACTIVE: staff contact providers; most accurate, most EXPENSIVE; outbreaks. PASSIVE: submitted reports; most COMMON; under-reporting.
SENTINEL: prearranged small group reports all cases. SYNDROMIC: clinical-feature case definitions (diarrhea, not cholera); commonest in developing countries.
Starts at LOCAL and STATE health departments; if notifiable → reported to the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention.
Required BY LAW to be reported; contagiousness, severity or frequency. Infectious, bioterrorism, sexually transmitted, NONINFECTIOUS (lead, carbon monoxide). List produced yearly.
Written: gonorrhea, salmonellosis · TELEPHONE: rubeola, pertussis · total number: chickenpox, influenza · cancer → state registries.

label: L12 · Morbidity, Mortality & Causation
rows: ALL cases present (odometer). Depends on incidence AND duration; used for chronic disease. Low = low incidence, rapidly fatal, or rapid recovery.
Crude (all causes) · cause-specific · age-specific · INFANT (compares countries) · maternal (pregnancy).
Deaths / total cases. Over-estimated early (sickest counted), under-estimated as mild cases are tested.
Association = exposure linked to disease frequency in POPULATIONS (risk factors). Causation = a true mechanism. Association does not make it causal.
Base → apex: chance · spurious/artifact · confounded · non-causal · CAUSAL.
Consistency · strength (relative risk very high or low) · BIOLOGICAL GRADIENT (dose-response; most reliable) · TEMPORAL (exposure first) · plausibility · coherence · specificity.

label: L12 · Epidemic Terms & Applications
rows: ENDEMIC: chronically low levels · SPORADIC: irregular or isolated · EPIDEMIC: in excess of expected · PANDEMIC: world-wide epidemic.
Common source: POINT (within 1 incubation period), continuous, intermittent · PROPAGATED: person to person · MIXED: source then spread · other: zoonotic, vector-borne.
R0: cases from one case, susceptible population, NO interventions. R: with interventions or immunity.
Cumulative number (or %) of IMMUNE people in a population; vaccination plus natural immunity.
Establish outbreak → prepare → VERIFY diagnosis → define cases → descriptive → hypothesis → evaluate → refine → control → COMMUNICATE.
Health department closed for the weekend · case-control: time in Hotel A's LOBBY · lab found the bacteria in specimens thought dead.
Surveillance (problem?) → risk factors (cause?) → intervention evaluation (what works?) → implementation (how?).
Values, ideology, politics, EVIDENCE (epidemiology's contribution; not usually the main influence). Cycle: assess health → assess interventions → choose → implement → evaluate.
Individual → COMMUNITY approach; secondhand smoke made it societal: smoke-free public places, less advertising, less youth access, higher taxes.
Income, poverty, race, discrimination, access to care · air/water pollution, hazardous waste sites · workers' injuries and illness → regulation.
